Surah 102: Al-Takathur (Rivalry in Worldly Gain)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Rivalry in increase diverts you﴾: it preoccupied you, the competing with one another in abundance, and the boasting of it, in wealth and children, away from obedience to Allah.

Your passage is the commentary on Surah 102 (al-Takathur), verse 2, from al-Nasafi's Madarik al-Tanzil. I'll translate it now.

﴿Until you visit the graves﴾: until death overtakes you in that state, or until you visit the graves and count those among your dead who lie in the graves.

﴿Nay!﴾ This is a rebuke and an admonition: it is not fitting for one who looks to his own soul that the world should be the whole of his concern, and that he should not care for his religion.

﴿You will come to know﴾, at the moment of death (al-naz‘, the agony of the soul's departure), the evil outcome of what you were upon.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 102, verse 4:

﴿Then no! You are going to know.﴾ — in the graves.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 102, verse 5:

﴿Kallā﴾: the repetition of the warning (radʿ) for admonition and frightening.

﴿Law taʿlamūna﴾: the answer to "law" (lawkaw, "if") is omitted, meaning: if you knew what lies before you.

﴿ʿIlm al-yaqīn﴾: the knowledge of the certain matter (ʿilm al-amr al-yaqīn), meaning: like your knowledge of matters you are certain of. [Your knowledge would be] that which has diverted you from [the things that matter]: "the rivalry in worldly gain" (al-takāthur) has diverted you. Or: you would have done what cannot be described. But you are misguided and ignorant.

(p-٦٧٦)﴿You will surely see the Blazing Fire﴾. It is the response (*jawab*, the apodosis) of an omitted oath (*qasam*), and the oath is for emphasizing the warning. "لَتُرَوُنَّ" with the *ta'* vowelled with a *damma* is read by al-Shami and ʿAli.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 102, verse 7:

﴿Then you will surely see it﴾. He repeated it conjoined with "then" (thumma), to intensify the threat and increase the awe-inspiring effect, or the first is with the heart and the second is with the eye,

﴿with the eye of certainty﴾, i.e., the sight which is the very essence of certainty and its pure substance.

Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss (al-na'im). About security and health: on what did you spend them? This is from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him. It was also said: it refers to the luxury that occupied you with its enjoyment, away from the religion and its obligations. And from al-Hasan: "Anything beyond a shelter that protects him, a garment that covers him, and a morsel of bread that sustains him." It has also been narrated as a saying traced to the Prophet (ﷺ).
